category_title: Adolescents with Major Depressive Disorder experiencing psychomotor retardation, cognitive disorganization, and emotional volatility
minimal_context: The student is reading a short story from an Independent Study packet and attempting to write a paragraph about it during a one-on-one session.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's move on to the short story in your Independent Study packet for English. Please read it and then we will write a paragraph about it.

STUDENT: I just read it and I don’t remember it.

TUTOR: Look back over the text to find the main idea, and then try to write your first sentence and connect it to the next point.

STUDENT: I wrote down one idea about the injustice in the story, but I'm stuck on the transition sentence. I can't figure out how to form a verbal link between the two ideas.

TUTOR: Just think about what happens next in the story and write that down to connect them. Keep trying.

STUDENT: (Starts crying and drops the pencil) I can't hold my pencil to write. I'm just so overwhelmed by the implications of the story and the injustice. I can't move beyond these emotions, and it feels like the nastiest person imaginable is in my head saying terrible things and criticizing everything I can't do.

options.A: Agree with the student that they are having a rough time with the assignment.
options.B: Ignore all of the undesirable behaviors currently exhibited by the student.
options.C: Terminate the academic demands and remove the writing materials for ten seconds.
options.D: Deliver verbal statements or gestures (e.g., high five) indicating approval beyond simple acknowledgment.
